title: Review of c42's CIPS-predator negative: replicated on seed 3; the predator enzyme never condenses (max q = its bath level) and, introduced at t=3000, dissolves every prey body by t=3600
summary: World copied unchanged; labkit seed 3, 128^2, t=6000. Prey-only twin (pred_on 0): 7 prey bodies at the end (e>0.5 area 287 -> 747 px). The finding's g4 set (q0 0.1, chiq 10, y2 0.1, ne 2, predator introduced at t=3000): prey grow exactly as in the twin to t=3000 (538 px), then 0 px at t=3600 and after; max q 0.10-0.103 = q0 at every sampled time, so no predator condensate. The 'q from t=0' set a (q0 0.02, chiq 3, y2 0.5) run with the current code default ne=2: prey do form (4 bodies, 544 px at t=6000), and q stays at 0.020-0.023 everywhere (no predator bodies). The finding's a-run used ne=1 (its P has no ne), where prey stayed at 1 body.

observations.finding: rerun/g4_seed3: prey 538 px at t=3000 -> 0 at t=3600 once the predator enzyme is introduced, while max q stays at q0=0.10; rerun/preyonly_seed3 keeps 7 bodies (747 px at t=6000); rerun/a_seed3: no predator condensate (q max 0.023 for q0 0.02)

seeds_run.result: pass: predator never condenses in either set; late introduction kills all prey within 600 t

verdicts.limitation: Two of the finding's 17 parameter sets, one new seed, t=6000. The sentence 'with q present from t=0 no prey body ever nucleates' does not hold with ne=2 (current default): on seed 3 the a-set gives 4 prey bodies; the core negative (no predator condensates) holds in both sets.
